0.headline: Ardee Industries IPO allotment today; check status on BSE, NSE and registrar, GMP at 30%
0.heading: Ardee Industries IPO allotment today; check status on BSE, NSE and registrar, GMP at 30%
0.intro: Ardee Industries is set to finalise the basis of allotment for its initial public offering (IPO) today, on August 10, following a strong response from investors during the three-day bidding period.
0.body:
Ardee Industries is set to finalise the basis of allotment for its initial public offering (IPO) today, on August 10, following a strong response from investors during the three-day bidding period.

The Rs 425.87 crore IPO was subscribed 133.66 times by the close of bidding on August 7. Investors placed bids for 7,80,68,45,689 equity shares against 5,84,22,516 shares on offer, according to the issue data.

The non-institutional investor (NII) category recorded the strongest demand, with the portion subscribed 255.22 times. The retail investor segment was subscribed 45.65 times.

The IPO opened on August 5 and closed on August 7. The price band was fixed at Rs 50-53 per share.

The grey market premium (GMP) for Ardee Industries has remained firm ahead of the expected allotment. According to InvestorGain and IPO Watch, the GMP was around Rs 16 per share on August 7. At the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 53, this implied a potential listing premium of about 30 percent.

Investors must note that the grey market premiums are unofficial and based on market speculation. They do not guarantee listing gains or reflect the company's fundamentals.

Ardee Industries is scheduled to list its shares on BSE and NSE on August 12, according to the tentative IPO timeline.

The public issue comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth Rs 320 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 1.99 crore shares by existing shareholders. The company plans to use Rs 220 crore from the fresh issue towards incremental working capital requirements and Rs 20 crore for repayment of certain borrowings. The remaining amount is earmarked for general corporate purposes.

Ahead of the IPO, the company raised about Rs 127.73 crore from anchor investors through the allotment of 2.41 crore equity shares at Rs 53 apiece.

Among the anchor investors, Bank of India Small Cap Fund, Bengal Finance &amp; Investment and Winro Commercial were allotted 47.17 lakh shares each. The Wealth Company Alternates Trust's Bharat Value Fund and India Max Investment Fund received 37.73 lakh shares each.

Cognizant Capital Dynamic Opportunities Fund and Catalyst New India Fund were allotted 12.03 lakh shares each.

Pantomath Capital Advisors is the book-running lead manager for the issue, while KFin Technologies is the registrar. The company's investor information also lists KFin Technologies as its registrar and transfer agent.

Check IPO News Here

How to check Ardee Industries IPO allotment status on BSE

Investors can check their allotment status on the BSE website once the basis of allotment is made available.

Step 1. Visit the BSE IPO allotment status page at https://www.bseindia.com/investors/appli_check
Step 2. Select Equity under issue type.
Step 3. Select Ardee Industries Ltd. from the issue-name dropdown.
Step 4. Enter the application number or PAN.
Step 5. Complete the captcha.
Step 6. Click on Search/Submit to view the allotment status.

How to check Ardee Industries IPO allotment status on NSE

Investors can also check their application details through the NSE IPO section.

1. Visit the NSE IPO application status page at https://www.nseindia.com/invest/check-trades-bids-verify-ipo-bids
2. Select Equity &amp; SME IPO bid details.
3. Select ARDEE from the company/symbol list.
4. Enter the required PAN and application details.
5. Submit the information to check the status.

How to check Ardee Industries IPO allotment status on KFin Technologies

KFin Technologies is the registrar for the Ardee Industries IPO. Investors can check their allotment through the registrar's portal using their PAN, application number or DP ID/client ID.

Step 1. Visit the KFin Technologies IPO allotment page at https://ipostatus.kfintech.com/
Step 2. Select Ardee Industries Ltd.
Step 3. Choose PAN, application number or DP ID/client ID.
Step 4. Enter the relevant details.
Step 5. Submit the form to view the allotment status.

The company has listed KFin Technologies' investor contact details, including the IPO email address ardee.ipo@kfintech.com, on its investor-relations page.

For investors who receive shares, the tentative timeline indicates that shares will be credited to demat accounts on August 11, while refunds or unblocking of funds for unsuccessful applicants are also expected from August 11. The stock is scheduled to debut on BSE and NSE on August 12.

About Ardee Industries

Ardee Industries is engaged in the recovery and recycling of end-of-life energy storage products and non-ferrous metal scrap. The company manufactures pure lead and lead alloys that are supplied to industries including energy storage, automotive, e-mobility and chemicals.

Disclaimer: The views and investment tips expressed by investment experts on Moneycontrol.com are their own and not those of the website or its management. Moneycontrol.com advises users to check with certified experts before making any investment decisions.

1.headline: Chart of the Day | Why retail has stopped chasing IPOs in 2026
1.heading: Chart of the Day | Why retail has stopped chasing IPOs in 2026
1.intro: SEBI's own study confirms what everyone suspected: retail IPO money is a trade, not an investment
1.body:
Retail investors have long treated IPOs as a short-term trade rather than a long-term bet, chasing listing day gains more than anything else. That pattern shows up clearly in 2026. An Axis Capital report shows that retail investment in IPOs has stayed low this year, even though gains have been marginally higher than in 2025 (see chart).


Source: Business Line, Axis Capital


Interestingly, market regulator SEBI is aware of this behaviour. A SEBI study on investor behaviour in mainboard IPOs found that individual investors sold roughly half their allotted shares within a week of listing, while non-institutional investors offloaded nearly two thirds of theirs in that same short window.

The study, based on 144 IPOs listed between April 2021 and December 2023, found that investors were far more eager to sell when an IPO listed with gains than when it listed flat or at a loss. When listing returns crossed 20 percent, individual investors dumped more than two thirds of their shares by value within a week. When returns turned negative, that selling dropped sharply, to well under 25 percent.

Retail money in IPOs is rarely about researching a company and holding on for the long term.

2026 has not been a good year for retail investors and traders. The secondary market has gone nowhere, IPO returns are low, and for derivative trading 2026 has been the worst year since derivatives were introduced in Indian markets. Secondary markets play an important role in shaping investor sentiment. When broader indices are choppy or under pressure, grey market premiums shrink.

Returns in the primary market were just 8 percent in 2025, only marginally higher in 2026, and as a result retail investors felt safer staying out. Geopolitical risks and high valuations also weighed on sentiment.

Of the 12 IPOs that hit the market in July, only five saw their retail portion oversubscribed in double digits, while six managed just single digit oversubscription. Even the Rs 9,275 crore Manipal Health Enterprises issue, the second largest of the year, saw its retail portion undersubscribed, receiving bids for only 93 percent of the shares on offer.

Average IPO applications per issue have fallen from 18.86 lakh in 2024 to just 9.85 lakh in 2026, largely because average listing gains dropped from 30 percent in 2024 to 12 percent in 2026.

High valuation is also a reason listing gains have come down. There is not much left on the table for primary market investors once merchant bankers and promoters price issues at levels that already factor in mid-term future earnings.

Besides valuation, another factor that has put off investors is the rise in Offer for Sale issues, where promoters and early investors cash out rather than the company raising fresh capital.

However, none of this is likely to be permanent. History suggests this cycle repeats itself. Between 2014 and 2017, average listing premiums fell from 20.8 percent to 6.3 percent before climbing back to 28.2 percent within three years. The same cycle played out between 2020 and 2022, when average listing gains slid from 43.8 percent to just 10 percent as retail investors pulled back once the listing gains disappeared. More recent examples came in late 2024 and mid-2025, when retail and HNI applications collapsed as listing gains halved, only to start recovering once a handful of issues began delivering healthy first day gains again.

Every time listing gains erode and applications shrink, issuers and bankers rework their valuations to revive demand, and retail money returns once the risk reward math improves. With the pace of new issuance already picking up and July recording the highest fundraising of the year so far, it may only take a handful of well-priced issues and strong listings to pull retail investors back into the queue.

2.headline: Business News Live: Molbio Diagnostics, Dhoot Transmission IPOs open today; crude oil, Maruti Suzuki, AI data centres in focus
2.heading: Business News Live: Molbio Diagnostics, Dhoot Transmission IPOs open today; crude oil, Maruti Suzuki, AI data centres in focus
2.intro: Bain Capital-backed automotive wiring harness manufacturer Dhoot Transmission's IPO also opens for subscription today and will close on August 12.
2.body:
Temasek and Motilal Oswal Group-backed Molbio Diagnostics' Rs 930.7-crore IPO opens for subscription today, August 10, and will close on August 12. The company has fixed the price band at Rs 768-807 per share, with investors able to bid for a minimum of 18 shares and in multiples thereafter.

Bain Capital-backed automotive wiring harness manufacturer Dhoot Transmission's IPO also opens for subscription today and will close on August 12. Ahead of the issue opening, the company allotted 1.05 crore equity shares to 72 anchor investors and raised Rs 918.27 crore.

The anchor book saw participation from several marquee domestic and global investors, including SBI Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential MF, HDFC MF, BlackRock, WhiteOak, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Axis MF, Mirae Asset, Nippon India MF, Government Pension Fund, Pictet, Amundi Funds, Allianz Global Investors, Franklin Templeton, Tata MF, Invesco, Canara Robeco, UTI MF, PGIM India MF, HSBC MF, Sundaram MF, SBI Life Insurance, HDFC Life Insurance, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, Axis Max Life Insurance, Motilal Oswal MF, Bandhan MF, Edelweiss MF and 3P India Equity Fund, among others.

Meanwhile, in other news: Crude oil prices rose moderately in early Asian trading today, August 10, while holding on to recent gains as traders awaited an agreement between Iran and Oman on managing shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude was trading near $85 a barrel after rising more than 5% over the past three sessions, while West Texas Intermediate was around $79 a barrel.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that an agreement with Oman to establish a shipping route through the key waterway was "very close", but ruled out direct talks with the US, accusing Washington of repeatedly violating the MoU signed in June.

Maruti Suzuki Chairman R.C. Bhargava has called for faster reforms and an easier business environment, urging political parties to support wealth-creating programmes while highlighting technology, competition and biogas as key priorities.

AI data centres: AI data centres do not require environmental clearance merely because of the nature of their operations, the government told Parliament. In a written response to Rajya Sabha MP Sudha Murty on August 6, Minister of State for Environment Kirti Vardhan Singh said AI data centres do not per se require environmental clearance under the Environmental Impact Assessment Notification, 2006. However, clearance is mandatory if a data centre qualifies as a large building, construction or township project under the notification.
